messages.body_plain:
This is a limitation of ggplot2 and the data will be pooled with only one legend. It would be fine if you want a consistent color legend.

But if your data were measured in different ways or have different units, you definitely want to provide different color palettes. However this is not supported by ggplot2 directly. The most easy solution IMO is to use cowplot.

For re-ordering your data according to the tree structure, you can refer to the discussion on https://groups.google.com/forum/?utm_medium=email&utm_source=footer#!msg/bioc-ggtree/LqRDK78m3U4/hg5Cdf_ZAwAJ.

Guanyang

messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

When I plot some data using ggtree, the out groups are on a very long branch length. The out groups are 75 and 76 in the example below.

I would like to keep the out groups in the tree but ignore their branch lengths to make presentation easier.

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-1WNmjsJgm-w/Worvy9UJzSI/AAAAAAAAAXs/Ny1zly0SsWYNB47fP3XhqhoQxDTUqrxhACLcBGAs/s1600/Rplot1.png>

When I collapse the nodes 75 and 76 it does improve the appearance. but the out groups are still on a long branch.

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-ij4rRSh_KhM/WorwQerho8I/AAAAAAAAAXw/RmYYtMRhfWMLMbyZQ7QMjCpSC2HSHaRQACLcBGAs/s1600/Rplot2.png>

Is it possible to produce a plot such as the one I created manually below where the branch lengths for the out groups is ignored

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-64ekmkrEsB8/WorwjlCDTNI/AAAAAAAAAX4/h6AJpRRvlis18Qt-OAryamXB4dRfYnZsQCLcBGAs/s1600/Rplot3.png>

The script I have used so far is below and example data attached. Any thoughts would be much appreciated

Cheers
Ollie

library(ggtree)

# read in data
x <- read.tree("long-branch-example.newick")

# create ggtree object
tree <- ggtree(x) + geom_tiplab(size = 2)

# plot tree
tree

# find node for outgroup
MRCA(x, tip =c("75", "76"))

# collapse outgroup node
tree <- collapse(tree, node = 151)

# plot resulting tree
tree

p$data[tree$data$node %in% c(75, 76), "x"] = mean(p$data$x)
print(p)
